results.title: Sage Research Methods - Within-Subjects Design
results.content: Sage Research Methods - Encyclopedia of Research Design - Within-Subjects Design. A within-subjects design refers to a study design where two or more measures are obtained from a sample of subjects. A split-plot design can encompass the advantages of both between-subjects and within-subjects factors and thus is commonly used in the social and behavioral sciences. By contrast, in within-subjects designs, individual differences can be separated from the error term, as the same subjects are observed under multiple conditions, and thus, each subject can serve as his or her own control. A practical implication of both the removal of individual differences from the error term and the collection of a larger number of observations from the same subjects is that statistical power can be increased to detect treatment effects in within-subjects designs. The logic behind the crossover design is that any main effect of order will be controlled for and, as a result, the crossover within-subjects design possesses stronger internal validity than a design without counterbalancing.
